study type: Mixed-methods (cross-sectional online survey and phone interviews)
exposure: Hospitalization for birth during COVID-19 pandemic
outcome: Mother-infant bonding (measured by Postnatal Bonding Questionnaire)
cohort: Mothers diagnosed with COVID-19 by PCR test and admitted to four maternity facilities in Qatar between May 2020 and January 2022.
finding: Mothers diagnosed with COVID-19 exhibited impaired postnatal bonding (mean score 12.0), which was significantly impacted by the pandemic, leading to increased maternal stress, reduced physical contact, and limited partner support.
mod_finding: Mode of birth, particularly instrumental deliveries, was correlated with postnatal bonding scores.
cross-section timing: Postnatal period (data collected between May 2020 and January 2022, specific timing relative to birth not specified)
